title: Full character tangent weights and coroot reflection recognition over a ring
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an additive abelian group, $G$ an $R$-group scheme with the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $i:D_R(M)	o G$ a homomorphism, using [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Scalar extension is pullback with its pulled-back group law. Write $\chi_m:D_R(M)	o D_R(\mathbf Z)=\mathbf G_m$ for the Hopf map $e_n\mapsto e_{nm}$ and $\lambda_
u:\mathbf G_m	o D_R(M)$ for $e_m\mapsto e_{
u(m)}$, where $
u\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Z)$. For an $R$-algebra $A$, use the actual tangent module $\mathfrak g_A=\operatorname{Lie}(G_A)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(e^*\Omega^1_{G_A/A},A)$ of [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation] and its dual-number tangent points. For every $A$-algebra $C$, project the scalar-extended tangent point $v_C$ to $G(C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)$. Define the full $m$-weight submodule as the $A$-span of the vectors $v\in\mathfrak g_A$ such that, for every $A$-algebra $C$ and $t\in D_R(M)(C)$, one has $i(t)v_Ci(t)^{-1}=v_C(\epsilon\mapsto\chi_m(t)\epsilon)$. The equations are linear, so this span equals their solution module. Evaluate $\chi_m(t)$ on the actual basis element $e_m$. For an $R$-field $F$, define the geometric-coroot reflection condition for $(\alpha,
u)$ to mean the existence of $n\in G_F(F)$ such that on every $F$-test scheme $W$ and $t\in D_R(M)_F(W)$, $n i_F(t)n^{-1}=i_F(t\lambda_{
u,F}(\chi_{\alpha,F}(t))^{-1})$. When $G_F$ is reductive, $D_R(M)_F$ is a maximal torus, $\alpha$ is a root and $
u(\alpha)=2$, this is the normalizer-reflection characterization of its usual coroot. All tests include nonreduced algebras and schemes.
